concepts.name: Tail recursion requires the self-call to be final

questions.prompt: A Kotlin recursive function returns `1 + visit(next)`. Why does adding `tailrec` fail to remove its recursive stack growth?

choices.text: The addition still runs after the recursive call returns
Returning an integer prevents optimization of recursive calls
A function parameter prevents optimization of recursive calls
The recursive call must appear at the start of the function

questions.explanation: The addition is work after the self-call, so that call is not the final operation. Returning integers or using parameters is allowed; placing recursion first does not make it tail recursion.

sources.title: Functions
sources.claim: A tailrec function is optimized into a loop when its self-call is the final operation; code after that call, try/catch/finally and open functions prevent tail recursion.

questions.prompt: An Android app persists `Status.ordinal` in its database. A release reorders the enum constants. Which design prevents old rows from silently changing meaning?

choices.text: Persist an explicit stable code assigned to each constant
Read the saved ordinal from the reordered `entries` collection
Persist the ordinal plus the current number of enum constants
Persist the ordinal after converting its value to a string

questions.explanation: Ordinal records declaration position, which changes on reordering. A stable explicit code preserves meaning; a count, entries lookup or string conversion leaves the same positional coupling.

sources.title: Enum classes
sources.claim: An enum ordinal is its zero-based declaration position; use an explicit code property for identifiers that must survive reordering, and valueOf requires an exact name.

questions.prompt: A Kotlin class defines `operator fun component1()` and `operator fun component2()` with logging. Consider `val (_, value) = item`. Which statements hold? Select all that apply.

choices.text: `component1()` is skipped for the underscore
The underscore shifts `component2()` into the first position
`component2()` supplies the value of `value`
Both component functions run before the first value is discarded
The variable name `value` selects a matching property by name

questions.explanation: Destructuring is positional: the second slot calls component2. An underscore suppresses its own component call, rather than discarding an already-computed value. Variable names do not select properties, and skipping a slot does not renumber later slots.

sources.title: Destructuring declarations
sources.claim: Destructuring uses operator componentN functions in positional order; an underscore skips the corresponding component function call.

questions.prompt: A Kotlin traversal has deep recursion and a self-call as its final operation. What does a valid `tailrec` modifier enable?

choices.text: Optimizing any recursion regardless of code after the self-call
Removing stack frames for every helper function the traversal calls
Launching each recursive invocation on a different worker thread
Compilation into a loop that avoids a frame for each self-call

questions.explanation: When its formal conditions hold, tailrec transforms self-recursion into a loop. It neither creates threads nor eliminates arbitrary helper calls, and post-call work prevents this optimization.

sources.title: Functions
sources.claim: A tailrec function is optimized into a loop when its self-call is the final operation; code after that call, try/catch/finally and open functions prevent tail recursion.

questions.prompt: A Kotlin enum stores `code: Int` for a wire protocol. The server sends one of those codes. Which lookup matches that protocol?

choices.text: Find the enum entry whose explicit `code` equals the received value
Compare the received value with each enum constant's `ordinal`
Pass the received numeric code as a string to the generated enum `valueOf`
Use the received value as an index into the current enum `entries`

questions.explanation: Explicit properties can represent stable protocol codes. entries indices and ordinal are declaration positions. valueOf looks up an exact enum name, not a numeric property.

sources.title: Enum classes
sources.claim: An enum ordinal is its zero-based declaration position; use an explicit code property for identifiers that must survive reordering, and valueOf requires an exact name.

questions.prompt: A Kotlin destructuring declaration is `val (label, id) = record`. Which statements describe its component mapping? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Variable names select matching record properties through reflection
The second slot receives the result of `component2()`
Component positions follow alphabetical ordering of property names
Reading `id` first reverses the order of the component function calls
The first slot receives the result of `component1()`

questions.explanation: Destructuring uses positional component functions: first component1, then component2. Local names, alphabetical property order and later reads do not alter that mapping.

sources.title: Destructuring declarations
sources.claim: Destructuring uses operator componentN functions in positional order; an underscore skips the corresponding component function call.
